definitions.explanation: A vast expanse of uncultivated, undeveloped land. Evokes images of untamed natural landscapes such as grasslands, plains, or scrubland.

examples.japanese: {広大|こうだい}な{原野|げんや}が{広|ひろ}がっている。
examples.english: A vast wilderness stretches out before us.

examples.japanese: {北海道|ほっかいどう}の{原野|げんや}を{馬|うま}で{駆|か}け{抜|ぬ}けた。
examples.english: I galloped through the wilderness of Hokkaido on horseback.

examples.japanese: かつての{原野|げんや}は{開拓|かいたく}されて{今|いま}では{農地|のうち}になっている。
examples.english: The former wilderness was cultivated and is now farmland.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{広大|こうだい}な{原野|げんや} (vast wilderness)
・{原野|げんや}を{開拓|かいたく}する (cultivate wild land)
・{原野|げんや}が{広|ひろ}がる (wilderness stretches out)

USAGE NOTES:
A literary word that conjures images of vast, untouched landscapes. Commonly associated with Hokkaido, which was historically undeveloped compared to mainland Japan. The word carries a slightly more poetic and literary feel than {荒野|こうや} (wasteland, desolate field), and unlike {荒野|こうや}, does not imply barrenness or desolation — {原野|げんや} can be lush and green.
